literal: when the consort was about to arrive he broke open the north gate of the city and went out ten li to welcome her.
idiomatic: but when the consort was about to arrive he had the north gate broken open and rode ten li out to welcome her.

literal: Again he fled with the consort to Qingzhou.
idiomatic: He fled again with the consort to Qingzhou.

literal: When the later lord reached Chang'an he begged Emperor Wu of Zhou for the consort; the emperor said: "I regard all under Heaven as cast-off shoes — would I begrudge an old woman to you!
idiomatic: When the later lord reached Chang'an he begged Emperor Wu of Zhou for the consort; the emperor said, "I regard all under Heaven as shoes I have cast off — would I begrudge you one old woman!

literal: " He still bestowed her on him.
idiomatic: " He gave her to him nonetheless.

literal: When the emperor met disaster the consort was bestowed on Prince of Dai Da; he was greatly infatuated with her.
idiomatic: When the later lord was killed the consort was given to Prince of Dai, Da, who doted on her greatly.

literal: The consort played the pipa; because a string broke she composed a poem: "Though I enjoy today's favor, I still recall former tenderness.
idiomatic: The consort was playing the pipa when a string snapped; she composed a poem: "Though I enjoy today's favor, I still recall former tenderness.

literal: If you wish to know the heart's severance, look at the glue on the broken string.
idiomatic: If you would know how the heart is severed, look at the glue on the broken string.

literal: " Da's consort was slandered by the consort and nearly came to death.
idiomatic: " Prince Da's own consort was slandered by her and nearly died for it.

literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was about to bestow her on Da's consort's brother Li Xun, he ordered her to wear cloth skirts and be paired to pound grain.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui was about to give her to Prince Da's consort's brother Li Xun, he ordered her to wear cloth skirts and be paired with him to pound grain at the mortar.

literal: Xun's mother forced her to kill herself.
idiomatic: Xun's mother drove her to suicide.

literal: The later lord took Li Zuqin's daughter as Left Zhaoyi and advanced her to Left Eying.
idiomatic: The later lord took Li Zuqin's daughter as Left Zhaoyi and promoted her to Left Eying.

literal: Lady Pei was Right Eying.
idiomatic: Lady Pei was made Right Eying.

literal: Eying — taking together the names of Shun's consorts Ehuang and Nuying — was Yang Xiuzhi's coinage.
idiomatic: The title Eying, combining the names of Shun's consorts Ehuang and Nuying, was Yang Xiuzhi's invention.

literal: Musician Cao Sengnu presented two daughters; the elder offended the will and had her face skinned;
idiomatic: The musician Cao Sengnu presented two daughters; the elder offended the emperor and had the skin of her face stripped away;

literal: the younger played the pipa and became zhaoyi.
idiomatic: the younger played the pipa and was made zhaoyi.

literal: Sengnu was made Prince of Rinan.
idiomatic: Sengnu was enfeoffed as Prince of Rinan.

literal: After Sengnu's death he again honored his brothers Miaoda and two others; on the same day all were made princes of commanderies.
idiomatic: After Sengnu died the emperor again favored his brothers Miaoda and two others; on a single day all three were made princes of commanderies.

literal: For the zhaoyi he separately raised Longji Hall, extremely ornate and beautiful.
idiomatic: For the zhaoyi he built a separate Longji Hall, lavish beyond measure.

literal: Lady Lu slandered her with left-hand ways and she was then killed.
idiomatic: Lady Lu accused her of sorcery and she was executed.

literal: There were also Consort Dong, Lady Mao, Lady Peng, Lady Wang, the Lesser Lady Wang, and two Ladies Li — all were greatly favored.
idiomatic: There were also Consort Dong, Lady Mao, Lady Peng, Lady Wang, the Lesser Lady Wang, and two Ladies Li — all were greatly favored.

literal: Mao could play the zither; she had originally been recommended by He Shikai.
idiomatic: Lady Mao could play the zither; He Shikai had originally recommended her.

literal: The emperor favored Lady Peng, who had also entered as a musical performer;
idiomatic: The emperor favored Lady Peng, who had entered the palace as a musical performer;

literal: she died at Jinyang; a Buddhist temple was built, rivaling the Zongchi.
idiomatic: she died at Jinyang, and a Buddhist temple was built to rival the Zongchi.

literal: One Li was the daughter of a bondservant household and entered with the five-string.
idiomatic: One Lady Li was the daughter of a bondservant household and was presented for her skill on the five-string.

literal: One Li was Xiaozheng's daughter.
idiomatic: The other Lady Li was Xiaozheng's daughter.

literal: The Lesser Wang bore one son; the eunuchs beside her all received gifts.
idiomatic: The Lesser Lady Wang bore a son; the eunuchs in attendance all received rewards.

literal: Mao's elder brother Sian was abruptly promoted to Martial Guard.
idiomatic: Lady Mao's elder brother Sian was abruptly promoted to the Martial Guard.

literal: Dong's father Xianyi was made army commander; through the zhaoyi he also abruptly rose to opening the government.
idiomatic: Consort Dong's father Xianyi was made an army commander; through his daughter he too was suddenly elevated to opening the government.

literal: The rest of the affinal kin mostly reached high office.
idiomatic: Other relatives by marriage likewise rose to high office.

literal: Northern Dynasties — Zhou
idiomatic: The Northern Dynasties: Zhou

literal: Empress Yuan of Zhou Wen was a younger sister of Emperor Xiaowu of Wei.
idiomatic: Empress Yuan of Zhou Wen was a younger sister of Emperor Xiaowu of Wei.

literal: At first enfeoffed Princess of Pingyuan, she was married to Zhang Huan, opening the government.
idiomatic: First enfeoffed as Princess of Pingyuan, she was married to Zhang Huan, a commander of the opening-the-government rank.

literal: Huan's nature was greedy and cruel; toward the empress he was without propriety.
idiomatic: Huan was greedy and cruel and treated the empress without proper respect.

literal: The emperor killed Huan and changed the empress's enfeoffment to Princess of Fengyi, matching her to Zhou Wendi.
idiomatic: The emperor executed Huan, changed her title to Princess of Fengyi, and gave her in marriage to Zhou Wendi.

literal: She bore Emperor Xiaomin.
idiomatic: She bore Emperor Xiaomin.

literal: In the seventeenth year of Great Unity of Wei she died.
idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Great Unity of Wei she died.

literal: In the twelfth month of the third year of the Gongdi era she was buried together at Chengling.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the third year of the Gongdi era she was buried with him at Chengling.

literal: When Xiaomin took the throne he posthumously honored her as queen.
idiomatic: When Xiaomin took the throne he posthumously honored her as queen.

literal: At the beginning of Wucheng she was again posthumously honored as empress.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Wucheng she was again posthumously honored as empress.

literal: Empress Chinu of Wenzuan was a man of Dai.
idiomatic: Empress Chinu of Wenzuan was from Dai.

literal: When Zhou Wendi was chief minister he took her as a concubine; she bore Wudi.
idiomatic: When Zhou Wendi was chief minister he took her as a concubine; she bore Wudi.

literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Tianhe she was honored as empress dowager.
idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year of Tianhe she was honored as empress dowager.

literal: In the third month of the third year of Jiande she died.
idiomatic: In the third month of the third year of Jiande she died.

literal: In the fifth month she was buried at Yonggu Tomb.
idiomatic: In the fifth month she was buried at Yonggu Tomb.

literal: Empress Dugu of Mingjing was the eldest daughter of Grand Guardian and Duke of Wei Xin.
idiomatic: Empress Dugu of Mingjing was the eldest daughter of the Grand Guardian and Duke of Wei, Xin.

literal: When the emperor was in his princedom he took her as lady.
idiomatic: When the emperor was still a prince he took her as his lady.

literal: In the first month of the second year she was established queen.
idiomatic: In the first month of the second year she was made queen.

literal: In the fourth month she died and was buried at Zhaoling.
idiomatic: In the fourth month she died and was buried at Zhaoling.

literal: At the beginning of Wucheng she was posthumously honored as empress.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Wucheng she was posthumously honored as empress.

literal: When Mingdi died she was buried together with the empress.
idiomatic: When Mingdi died she was buried together with him.

literal: Empress Ashina of Wucheng was the daughter of the Türk qaghan Muqan, son of Qaghan.
idiomatic: Empress Ashina of Wucheng was the daughter of the Türk qaghan Muqan.

literal: After the Türk destroyed the Rouran they wholly possessed the lands beyond the frontier; their ambition reached into the central plains.
idiomatic: After the Türk destroyed the Rouran they held all the lands beyond the frontier and turned their ambition toward the central plains.

literal: Zhou Wen was then contending with the Qi.
idiomatic: Zhou Wen was then locked in rivalry with Northern Qi.

literal: He allied with them as aid.
idiomatic: He allied with the Türk for support.

literal: Qaghan at first wished to give his daughter to the emperor, then afterward regretted it.
idiomatic: Qaghan at first intended to give his daughter to the Zhou emperor, then changed his mind.

literal: When Wudi took the throne envoys were repeatedly sent.
idiomatic: When Wudi took the throne envoys were sent again and again.

literal: In the second month of the fifth year of Baoding an edict ordered Duke of Chen Chun,
idiomatic: In the second month of the fifth year of Baoding an edict ordered the Duke of Chen, Chun,

literal: Duke of Xu Yu Wengui, Duke of Shenwu Dou Yi, Duke of Nan'an Yang Jian, and others, to prepare the empress's ritual objects and traveling hall, together with the six palaces below — one hundred twenty persons — and go to Qaghan's camp to welcome the empress.
idiomatic: the Duke of Xu Yu Wengui, the Duke of Shenwu Dou Yi, the Duke of Nan'an Yang Jian, and others to prepare the empress's ritual regalia and traveling pavilion, together with the full six-palace retinue of one hundred twenty persons, and proceed to Qaghan's camp to welcome the empress.

literal: Qaghan again promised marriage to Qi and was about to harbor a different intent; Chun and the rest repeatedly requested but could not return with their mission accomplished.
idiomatic: Qaghan also promised his daughter to Qi and was about to shift allegiance; Chun and the others pleaded repeatedly but could not obtain leave to return.

literal: Thunder and wind suddenly arose and blew down their yurt; Qaghan was greatly afraid, taking it as heaven's punishment, and then with ritual sent off the empress; Chun and the rest escorted her back.
idiomatic: Suddenly thunder and wind arose and blew down their yurt; Qaghan was terrified, taking it as heaven's punishment, and then ceremonially sent the empress off; Chun and the others escorted her home.

literal: In the third month of the third year of Tianhe she arrived; Wudi received her with the rites of greeting the bride in person.
idiomatic: In the third month of the third year of Tianhe she arrived; Wudi received her with the rites of personally greeting the bride.

literal: The empress had beauty and grace in bearing; the emperor deeply honored and treated her with ritual.
idiomatic: The empress was beautiful and graceful in deportment; the emperor treated her with deep respect and ceremony.

literal: When Xuandi took the throne the empress was honored as empress dowager.
idiomatic: When Xuandi took the throne she was honored as empress dowager.

literal: In the second month of the first year of Daxiang she was changed to Heavenly Yuan Empress Dowager.
idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Daxiang she was styled Heavenly Yuan Empress Dowager.

literal: In the second month of the second year she was again honored as Heavenly Yuan Supreme Empress Dowager.
idiomatic: In the second month of the second year she was further honored as Heavenly Yuan Supreme Empress Dowager.

literal: When Xuandi died Jingdi honored her as grand empress dowager.
idiomatic: When Xuandi died, Jingdi honored her as grand empress dowager.

literal: In the second year of Kaihuang of Sui she died, age thirty-two.
idiomatic: In the second year of Kaihuang under the Sui she died, aged thirty-two.

literal: Emperor Wen of Sui ordered the authorities to prepare rites and bury her attached at Xiaoling.
idiomatic: Emperor Wen ordered the authorities to prepare rites and bury her beside Xiaoling.

literal: Empress Yang of Xuandi, named Lihua, was the eldest daughter of Emperor Wen of Sui.
idiomatic: Empress Yang of Xuandi, named Lihua, was the eldest daughter of Emperor Wen of Sui.

literal: When the emperor was in the eastern palace Wudi had the emperor take her as crown prince's consort.
idiomatic: While the emperor was crown prince, Wudi had him take her as crown princess.

literal: In the intercalary sixth month of the first year of Xuanzheng she was together established empress.
idiomatic: In the intercalary sixth month of the first year of Xuanzheng she was made empress together with him.

literal: The emperor and empress each styled themselves Heavenly Yuan Emperor and Heavenly Yuan Empress.
idiomatic: The emperor and empress each styled themselves Heavenly Yuan Emperor and Heavenly Yuan Empress.

literal: Soon he also established Heavenly Empress and Left and Right empresses — four empresses in all.
idiomatic: Soon he also established a Heavenly Empress and Left and Right empresses — four empresses in all.

literal: In the second month of the second year an edict took the four stars as model; thereupon the empress and the three empresses all received greater titles.
idiomatic: In the second month of the second year an edict took the four stars as its model; the empress and the three other empresses all received elevated titles.

literal: The empress was invested as Heavenly Yuan Great Empress; he also established Heavenly Central Great Empress — five empresses in all.
idiomatic: The empress was invested as Heavenly Yuan Great Empress; a Heavenly Central Great Empress was also established — five empresses in all.

literal: The empress's nature was gentle and yielding, without jealousy; the four empresses and consorts all loved and looked up to her.
idiomatic: The empress was gentle and unjealous; the four empresses and all the consorts loved and revered her.

literal: The emperor afterward grew ever more violent and depraved; joy and anger lost measure.
idiomatic: The emperor grew ever more violent and depraved; his moods knew no bounds.

literal: Once he reproached the empress and wished to punish her; the empress in advancing and withdrawing was detailed and composed, in words and color unbending.
idiomatic: Once he reproached the empress and meant to punish her; she remained composed in bearing and unyielding in tone.

literal: The emperor was greatly angered and then ordered the empress to die, forcing her to take her own life.
idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and ordered her to die, forcing her to kill herself.

literal: The empress's mother Lady Dugu heard of it, went to the gate to plead guilt, knocked her head until it bled, and only then was she spared.
idiomatic: Her mother Lady Dugu heard of it, went to the palace gate to plead, knocked her head until it bled, and only then was the empress spared.

literal: When the emperor died Jingdi honored the empress as empress dowager; she dwelt in Hongsheng Palace.
idiomatic: When the emperor died Jingdi honored her as empress dowager; she lived in Hongsheng Palace.

literal: Earlier when Xuandi was ill he ordered Emperor Wen of Sui to enter the forbidden quarters to attend his illness.
idiomatic: Earlier, when Xuandi fell ill, he had summoned Emperor Wen of Sui into the inner palace to attend him.

literal: At the approach of death Liu Fang and Zheng Yi and others through a forged edict had Emperor Wen of Sui receive the testamentary regency.
idiomatic: As death approached, Liu Fang and Zheng Yi forged an edict placing Emperor Wen of Sui in charge as regent.

literal: The empress at first had not taken part in the plot, yet because the heir was young she feared power would rest in another clan, not benefiting herself; when she heard Fang and Yi had already carried out this edict her heart was greatly pleased.
idiomatic: The empress had not plotted at first, but because the heir was young she feared power would pass to another house; when she learned Fang and Yi had already issued the edict she was greatly pleased.

literal: Later she knew Emperor Wen harbored a different design and her heart was quite uneasy.
idiomatic: Later, when she saw that Emperor Wen harbored designs of his own, she grew uneasy.

literal: When the abdication was carried out her anger and grief grew ever greater.
idiomatic: When the throne was seized her anger and grief only deepened.

literal: Emperor Wen inwardly was deeply ashamed toward her.
idiomatic: Emperor Wen felt deep shame toward her in his heart.

literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang she was enfeoffed Princess of Leping.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaihuang she was enfeoffed as Princess of Leping.

literal: Later they again discussed seizing her will; the empress swore she would not permit it and they stopped.
idiomatic: Later there was talk of forcing her to remarry; she swore she would never consent, and the plan was dropped.

literal: In the fifth year of Daye she followed Emperor Yang to Zhangye and died in Hexi.
idiomatic: In the fifth year of Daye she accompanied Emperor Yang to Zhangye and died in Hexi.

literal: An edict ordered return to the capital; the authorities prepared rites and buried her attached at Dingling.
idiomatic: An edict ordered her remains returned to the capital; the authorities prepared rites and buried her beside Dingling.

literal: Xuandi's empress Zhu, named Manyue, was a man of Wu.
idiomatic: Xuandi's empress Zhu, named Manyue, was from Wu.

literal: Her family because of a case was confiscated and entered the eastern palace.
idiomatic: Her family, implicated in a crime, was confiscated and she was sent into the eastern palace.

literal: When Xuandi was crown prince the empress was chosen to manage clothing; the emperor summoned and favored her; she then bore Jingdi.
idiomatic: When Xuandi was crown prince she was chosen to manage his wardrobe; he summoned and favored her, and she bore Jingdi.

literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Daxiang she was established Heavenly Yuan Imperial Empress.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Daxiang she was made Heavenly Yuan Imperial Empress.

literal: In the seventh month she was changed to Heavenly Empress.
idiomatic: In the seventh month she was restyled Heavenly Empress.

literal: In the second month of the second year she was again changed to Heavenly Great Empress.
idiomatic: In the second month of the second year she was again restyled Heavenly Great Empress.

literal: The empress was originally not of a good family; she was also more than ten years older than the emperor — distant, lowly, without favor.
idiomatic: She was not from a respectable family and was more than ten years older than the emperor — kept at a distance, low in rank, without favor.

literal: Because of Jingdi she was especially honored; her rank was second only to Empress Yang.
idiomatic: Because of Jingdi she was specially honored; her rank stood just below Empress Yang.

literal: When Xuandi died Jingdi honored the empress as imperial empress dowager.
idiomatic: When Xuandi died Jingdi honored her as imperial empress dowager.
